item.title: Republican Midterm Redistricting Now Looks Like a Blunder
item.description: President Donald Trump’s mid-decade redistricting war is shaping up to be a strategic blunder. At the president’s urging, Republicans gerrymandered new maps based on Trump’s 2024 performance, wrongly assuming the midterm electorate would match his presidential coalition. Now, once-durable Republican strongholds that were redrawn for partisan gain have become fragile, forcing Republicans to direct resources to districts they thought would be solidly red.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: US Midterm Elections Could Be a Bumpy Ride for Both Parties
item.description: The gas isn’t cheap, but the journey is worth it — as long as you stay away from lizards named Meatball.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Green Carmichael

item.title: Democrats Shouldn’t Get Too Excited About Those Independent Candidates
item.description: The closer we get to the end of the midterms, the more polls seem to show that Republicans won’t just lose, but lose in a rout. Some of the latest have Democrats winning as many as 240 seats in the House and easily retaking control of the Senate. Indeed, Democrats believe this is their year.
item.dc:creator: Erika D. Smith
